title: Input, processing, output
description:
Every program has the shape from the lesson: **input**, **processing**, **output**. Write one in Python.

Read a name and a year of birth, then print a greeting and how old the person turns in 2026:

```
What is your name? Ada
What year were you born? 1815
Hello, Ada! In 2026 you turn 211.
```

The Python you need:

| Code | Does |
|---|---|
| `name = input("What is your name? ")` | Shows the question, waits for a line, and keeps what was typed in `name` (as text) |
| `year = int(input("..."))` | The same, then turns the text into a whole number with `int`, so you can do sums with it |
| `print("Hello,", name)` | Prints its values with a space between them |
| `print(f"Hello, {name}!")` | An f-string: values inside `{}` are put into the text |

starter.main.py:
name = input("What is your name? ")
print("Hello,", name)

solution.main.py:
name = input("What is your name? ")
year = int(input("What year were you born? "))
age = 2026 - year
print(f"Hello, {name}! In 2026 you turn {age}.")

hints: `input` always gives you text. `int(...)` turns `"1815"` into the number 1815, so `2026 - year` works.
